name: Settings toggles
what: A phone-settings card of glass under your chin: it pops in, then its switches flip on one after another - each row lights up as if pressed, the knob slides with a stretch and the track fills with colour and glows; it floats while it holds, a band of light crosses the glass, and it sinks away at the end.
origin: Rebuilt after the apple-toggles effect of claude-video-effects (MIT): a settings card whose switches turn on one by one - MotionLab's own code, a glass card made part of the shot
motion: f0-f11 the card pops in from 60 % with a small overshoot, rising 43 px (seen within 3 f); the switches flip from f14, one every gap (12) frames: a press lights the row (3 f in, 10 f out), the knob slides 7 f (slow end) stretching 1.32x mid-way while the track fills with the accent and glows; it floats 3 px while it holds; a band of light crosses the glass 24 f (S-curve) after the last flip; the last 9 f it sinks 30 px and fades (accelerating)

tracks.name: card in
tracks.what: the glass card pops in, rising into place

tracks.name: sheen
tracks.what: a band of light crosses the glass

tracks.name: card out
tracks.what: the card sinks away and fades

min_frames: start + round((20 + max(1, min(6, parts(rows))) * max(3, gap)) * fps / 30)
min_why: the last switch has to flip on (and be seen on) before it ends
